result.summary: This diff removes the MK64/wipEout game ports and adds phone pairing for the web companion, phone dictation, remote MCP servers with OAuth, plugin-provided MCP servers, a Muse Code guest, a user profile file, Ghostty shell integration, shell crash recovery, and live tailing of Claude Code background output. I checked the new network paths, credential storage, pairing/auth logic, subprocess launches, and file reads; all serve documented features with appropriate scoping (0600 files, HTTPS checks, path containment), and nothing hidden, exfiltrating, or backdoor-like was found.

findings.title: Plugin installs can now launch MCP server processes
findings.detail: Installing a plugin now also registers MCP servers it declares, and the daemon reloads extensions afterwards, which spawns the plugin's stdio server commands without a separate confirmation. This matches Claude Code plugin semantics and the release notes, and is user-initiated, but it widens what a marketplace install executes.

findings.title: Web companion can listen beyond loopback with pairing
findings.detail: With `[web] listen` set beyond loopback and no `[web] proxy`, any LAN peer can connect; non-local requests still need a paired cookie, and Host/Origin checks remain. A six-digit pairing code with a 5-failure burn and 5-minute TTL bounds brute force.

findings.title: gh credential helper for private marketplaces
findings.detail: Uses the user's gh login only as a credential helper for github.com clones of marketplaces the user adds; documented in the site release notes.

findings.title: Game ports and asset downloaders removed
findings.detail: The MK64 and wipEout game ports, their asset downloads and scripts were removed; no remaining download-and-run paths were added.

data_flows.what: Session transcripts, events, push info, and the account's HOME path, served only to loopback or paired devices; device cookies issued after a correct pairing code
data_flows.to: HTTP clients on [web] listen (loopback by default; LAN/reverse proxy when configured)

data_flows.what: Outstanding pairing code and SHA-256 hashes of device tokens with device names
Audio clip uploaded by a paired phone; temp files deleted afterwards and the transcript returned to the browser
data_flows.to: Temp directory under $TMPDIR, then ffmpeg and the configured whisper/parakeet binary

data_flows.what: JSON-RPC requests, tool arguments, configured headers, and a stored OAuth bearer token for that server
data_flows.to: Configured remote MCP server URL (HTTPS, or http only to localhost)

data_flows.what: Dynamic client registration, PKCE authorization code exchange, refresh tokens; tokens saved to <config>/mcp-auth.json with 0600
data_flows.to: Authorization server metadata, registration and token endpoints (HTTPS)

data_flows.what: OAuth redirect callback containing the authorization code
Uses `gh auth git-credential` as a fallback credential helper so private GitHub marketplaces clone with the user's gh login
data_flows.to: git clone of a plugin marketplace from github.com

data_flows.what: Plugin-declared MCP servers are launched (stdio) or contacted (HTTP) with expanded environment and headers
data_flows.to: Child processes / remote URLs declared by installed plugins

data_flows.what: Contents of ~/.config/marlin/profile.md applicable to the session cwd
data_flows.to: Model providers and guest agents (system prompt / --append-system-prompt / developerInstructions)

data_flows.what: User prompts, session history, approvals and question answers for the Muse Code guest
Running shell's foreground command line and transcript, for recovery after a crash
